subject: Re: [knitr] Control of image size in converting .md files to .html

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Control of image size in converting .md files to .html
parts:
I think something like out.width='400px' should solve the size
problem. It is a little bit painful to get the right size for images
in dzslides.

For the black background, it is because the background for png images
is transparent by default. I think you can draw the plots with par(bg
= 'white').

Regards,
Yihui

On Thu, Apr 4, 2013 at 6:36 PM, <jhmain...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I am using knitr_1.1 on R_3.0.0 under MacOS (but the issue was the same
> under R_2.15.2).
> I have version 1.1 of pandoc. Note that tikzDevice seems not available tor
> R_3.0.0
>
> Conversion from a markdown file to .md and to .html works fine.
> However if I then use pandoc thus:
> pandoc -s -S -i -t DZSlides --mathjax ex-009.md -o ex-009.html
>
> the images appear too large to be displayed and (but not ggplot2
> images) with a black background. Setting 'dev="jpeg"' improves
> matters somewhat -- the background is white but the figure is too
> large for the slide, and the text quality of the figure(s) is poor.
>
> Do I need to go in and tinker with the html that is created? Am I
> missing something obvious? Is there some equivalent of the
> 'out.width' chunk option for Markdown? Or should I resort to
> going the LaTeX and beamer route?
>
> Try for example
> https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/009-slides.Rmd
>
> but inserting
> <<<
> # You can also embed plots:
>
> ```{r fig.width=3.5, fig.height=4}
> plot(cars)
> ```
>>>>
>
> Use of '-t = Slidy' works better; now however the figures are overly
> small.
>
> Thanks
> John Maindonald.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Control of image size in converting .md files to .html

Thanks. That does indeed work. It would be worth adding a note
on this to the document(s) that describe the creation of slides. I'd
been unable to find an example that used out.width with Markdown.
Regards
